title: Uatu Haco — Osso-Gori exclave is Makasae, not Midiki
body: Suco-wide census data suggests strong Midiki dominance, but aldeia-level fieldwork records show Osso-Gori (620 people) and Lia-Bala (857 people) are actually Makasae-speaking. The true split is closer to 58% Midiki / 42% Makasae. Osso-Gori is a genuine geographic exclave — a separate polygon piece cut off by neighboring suco Uai-Oli — shown here at its own centroid. Lia-Bala is contiguous with the rest of the suco on the ground, but the shapefile does not preserve it as a separate piece, so it cannot be mapped separately (only flagged here in text).

title: Bado-Ho'o — Uai-Bobo and Uai-Cana exclave is Makasae, not Midiki
body: Aldeia-level fieldwork records show Uai-Bobo (676 people) and Uai-Cana (284 people) are Makasae-speaking rather than Midiki. The true split is closer to 69% Midiki / 31% Makasae. Both Makasae aldeias fall inside the suco's one mappable exclave, shown here at its own centroid — unlike Uatu Haco's Lia-Bala, this correction is fully captured by the geometry.

title: Builale — aldeia-level attribution still an open task
body: The largest combined Kairui-Midiki suco nationally. Aldeia population data has been obtained (5 aldeias, suco-office board total 2,319 vs. census total 2,194 — different collection dates, both real), but no aldeia-level language attribution has been confirmed yet. The map currently shows a uniform population-weighted split (87.1% Kairui+Midiki applied identically to every aldeia), explicitly a placeholder — both Uatu Haco and Bado-Ho'o turned out to have real internal variation once checked, so this figure should not be trusted at the aldeia level yet.

title: Uai-Mori — geometry corrected (2026-08)
body: Resolved by a site visit (the author physically traveled through neighboring sucos Fatulia and Liaruca to reach it): the shapefile had filed the real, small, northern Uai-Mori as an unlabeled disconnected piece of neighboring Bibileo's polygon, while a separate, larger central-Viqueque polygon was mislabeled "Uai Mori." Both sucos matched their shapefile entries by exact name, so this was an error in the source geometry, not the matching pipeline. Fix: Uai-Mori's geometry is now Bibileo's former disconnected northern piece; Bibileo's geometry is reduced to its remaining southern piece. Census attributes are unchanged for both sucos — only which polygon each is drawn with changed.
